title: All-hands March 2026 - talking points + Q&A (draft)
content:
Purpose / TL;DR:
- Prep notes for March all-hands (30 min keynote + 15 min live Q&A).
- Goal: Share product progress (hosted API, Dedicated, Private), operational milestones, and a few customer/metrics highlights.

Agenda (30 min):
1) Quick company health + metrics (3 min)
   - Usage growth: monthly active API keys +12% MoM (highlight top-of-funnel).
   - Cost/unit improvements: avg token cost down ~18% vs Nov 2025 after batching/kv cache improvements.
2) Product highlights (10 min)
   - Redwood Dedicated: GA of configurable autoscaling policies + burst pools (rolled to ~20 early customers in pilot).
     * Talking point: predictable throughput for enterprise customers, SLA-backed latency targets.
     * Ops note: still tuning cold-start behavior for multi-model nodes.
   - Redwood Private: VPC control plane beta — first two customers onboarding this quarter.
     * Talking point: private control plane + KMS integration for regulated workloads.
     * Open question: finalize on-prem installer packaging timeline (TBD).
   - Redwood Optimize: batching/quantization recommendations now surfaced in Console.
     * Impact: expected 10-25% unit cost savings depending on workload.
3) Engineering wins (5 min)
   - Serving runtime: new kernel selection improved 99th-pct latency by ~150ms for long-context workloads in internal benchmarks.
   - Observability: token-level cost breakdown is live in prod for all hosted customers.
4) People & org updates (3 min)
   - New hires: welcome to two infra engineers (names in HR email).
   - Hiring priorities: SRE, product lead for Optimize.
5) Closing + Live Q&A (9-10 min)

Key talking points (bullet-friendly):
- Mission reminder: Make high-performance, reliable LLM inference accessible — focus on serving & economics.
- We shipped Dedicated autoscaling and Private VPC beta — big step toward enterprise readiness.
- Team wins on latency/cost improvements — measurable impact for customers.
- Console improvements = better visibility for product & CS teams to show ROI.

Anticipated Q&A (prep answers):
Q: When will Private be generally available / support on-prem?
A: Beta for Private VPC is underway; GA timeline depends on a few infra milestones (packaging, installer validation, and a final audit). Rough target: end of Q2. We will share a clear timeline next month once we complete the on-prem testing run.

Q: What does Dedicated pricing look like for reserved capacity?
A: Pricing model remains commit-based (monthly/annual). We’re finalizing packaging tiers (small/medium/large GPU pools) and will publish guidance with sample unit economics and common workload patterns in the pricing doc next week (link in Confluence).

Q: How do fallbacks work if a model variant is unavailable?
A: Smart routing will automatically fall back to compatible model variants by policy (latency/cost/region). Fallback behavior is configurable per-route in Console; default policy favors availability with a quality guardrail.

Q: Any near-term risks we should expect?
A: Two items to call out: 1) Cold-start behavior for multi-model nodes (engineering working on pre-warm heuristics), 2) Packaging/on-prem timeline for Private. We’ll update endpoints and docs as mitigations land.

Notes to self / TODOs before All-Hands:
- Finalize slides: product screenshots, Dedicated autoscaling diagram, Optimize UX flow (who owns slide?).
- Pull one customer quote from CS (ask Samira).
- Confirm hiring slides with People Ops (Asha).
- Figure out short demo: quick Console tour showing token-level cost breakdown + routing policy UI (keep demo <3 min).
- Rehearse Q&A responses with execs (schedule 30-min dry run).

Unresolved / open items (callouts):
- On-prem installer: need sign-off from security/compliance - who to ping? (security-and-compliance team contact).
- Dedicated: finalize SLA numbers in public docs (ops/legal alignment).
- Metrics: pull exact numbers for 99th-pct latency improvement and cost delta from observability team (Emil to confirm).

Tone guidance for speaker:
- Keep it concise, product-first, celebrate engineering wins, be transparent about risks and timelines.
- Use one concrete customer story to ground the product impact.

Rough slide outline (for design):
- Title slide: Company/All-hands Mar 2026
- TL;DR: 3 bullets (Product wins, Metrics, People)
- Product slides (Dedicated, Private, Optimize) - 1 slide each with 1 metric & 1 next-step
- Engineering wins + metrics slide
- People & hiring slide
- Closing & Q&A slide

Linked artifacts / refs:
- Product update Confluence (full notes): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ALL-2026-03-product-update
- Draft of tweet-sized customer quote: GH PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/announcements/pull/89
- Jira for Private packaging: JIRA-1234

Misc scratch/phrases to consider in slides:
- "Serving > owning" line (short manifest for mission slide).
- "Predictable performance, everywhere" (for Dedicated + Private message).
- Demo idea: show token-level cost breakdown for a simple 2-route app and flip routing policy to show cost vs latency tradeoff.

End of draft.

(Notes: this is a working scratchpad — expect edits. Will trim bullets to fit 30-min slot.)
